structure.lemma: REPAIR OF THE JOINT COUNT FOR CONSTANT q (partial; does NOT close G0001, G0002 or G0004). Let f = g_1 xor ... xor g_q over a fixed variable order, with g_i(x) = [W_i . x >= t_i] single threshold gates, and prefix length l, k = n - l. Then for every l: K_l(f) <= min(2^l, (2^k + 1)^q), and so sum_l K_l(f) <= (n+1) 2^{q(n+1)/(q+1)}.
structure.proved_step: PROOF. Fix a prefix a in {0,1}^l and write theta_i(a) = t_i - W_i1 . a. The residual of g_i is y -> [W_i2 . y >= theta_i(a)], which depends only on the cell of theta_i(a) among the sorted subset sums of W_i2 (at most 2^k values, hence at most 2^k + 1 cells). So the residual of f is determined by the tuple of q cell indices, giving at most (2^k+1)^q distinct residuals; trivially K_l <= 2^l. Since 2^k + 1 <= 2^{k+1}, min(2^l, 2^{q(n-l+1)}) is maximised when l = q(n+1-l), with value 2^{q(n+1)/(q+1)} (real maximum of min(l, q(n+1-l))). Summing over the n+1 levels gives the bound. CONSEQUENCE: for constant q, sum_l K_l <= (n+1) 2^{qn/(q+1) + O(1)} = 2^n / n^{omega(1)}, saving a factor 2^{-n/(q+1)}. For q = 2m with m bottom gates per circuit, the exponent q/(q+1) tends to 1 as m grows, so the bound becomes trivial at m = n^1.5 (this is the G0004 obstacle). Status: not source-checked, may already be known in the OBDD literature. Checked numerically in the next run.

structure.proved_step:
statement: Let f = XOR_{i=1..q} g_i on {0,1}^n, where g_i(x) = [w_i . x >= t_i], w_i in Z^n with |w_ij| <= B, t_i in Z. Let M = 2Bn+2. For every l in {0..n}, the number K_l of distinct residual functions f|_{x_1..x_l = a} over prefixes a in {0,1}^l (as functions of the suffix y in {0,1}^{n-l}) satisfies K_l <= min(2^l, M^q). Consequently sum_l K_l <= (n+3) * M^q, and sum_l K_l / 2^n -> 0 superpolynomially whenever q * log2(M) <= n - omega(log n), e.g. q = o(n / log n) with B = O(1).
proof: Fix a prefix a. Write w_i = (p_i, v_i) with p_i the prefix part and v_i the suffix part, k = n-l. The residual of g_i is [v_i . y >= c_i(a)] with c_i(a) = t_i - p_i . a, an integer. Since |v_i . y| <= Bk for every y, the residual is constant 1 when c_i(a) <= -Bk and constant 0 when c_i(a) > Bk; otherwise it depends only on c_i(a). So the residual of g_i depends only on c_i(a) clamped to {-Bk, ..., Bk+1}, which has at most 2Bk+2 <= M values. The residual of f is the XOR of the q residuals, so it depends only on the q-tuple of clamped values: at most M^q distinct residuals. Also K_l <= 2^l trivially. For the sum: let L = q log2 M. Levels l <= L contribute at most sum 2^l <= 2^(L+1) = 2M^q. Each of the at most n+1 levels with l > L contributes at most M^q. Total <= (n+3) M^q. The last claim follows from (n+3) M^q / 2^n = 2^{q log M - n + O(log n)}.
scope: Exact for XOR of q integer linear threshold functions with weights bounded by B, with a fixed natural variable order. Bookkeeping lemma: it does NOT close G0001 or G0002. It does not apply to THR o THR with m = n^alpha bottom gates, where q = Theta(n^1.5) and M^q is far above 2^n, so the bound is trivial there. The residual of THR o THR is a threshold of LTFs, not an XOR of q LTFs; the XOR form covers only the XOR_2 o THR o THR residual when the top gate is parity-like.

structure.lemma: SUBCLASS LEMMA (read-once contiguous blocks). Variables x_1..x_n in natural order. Blocks B_1..B_m partition [n] into intervals, g_j(x) = [W_j . x_{B_j} >= t_j] with integer weights, top gate f(x) = [sum_j v_j g_j(x) >= T]. S = sum_j |v_j|, b = max_j |B_j|. For each level l, K_l = number of distinct residual functions f|rho over the 2^l prefixes rho of x_1..x_l. Then K_l <= min(2^l, (S+1)(2^r+1)), where r = number of unread variables of the block containing position l (r = 0 at block boundaries). Hence sum_l K_l <= n(S+1)(2^b+1).
structure.proved_step: PROOF. Fix l and a prefix rho. (i) Blocks entirely before the cut block B are fixed by rho, so c(rho) = sum over those blocks of v_j g_j is an integer in [sum min(0,v_j), sum max(0,v_j)], an interval of width at most S, so c takes at most S+1 values. (ii) Blocks entirely after B are untouched by rho. (iii) Write x_B = (a, y), a the read part, y in {0,1}^r unread. Then g_B = [W2 . y >= theta(rho)] with theta(rho) = t_B - W1 . a. So f|rho(z,y) = [c(rho) + v_B [W2 . y >= theta(rho)] + sum_{j after B} v_j g_j(z) >= T]. (iv) The vector s(y) = W2 . y takes at most 2^r values, so the threshold functions [s(y) >= theta] over all integers theta form at most 2^r+1 distinct functions. (v) So the residual is determined by the pair (c(rho), threshold class of theta(rho)), giving K_l <= (S+1)(2^r+1); also K_l <= 2^l. Summing over l with r <= b gives the stated sum bound. CONSEQUENCE: #SAT of f by dynamic programming over blocks with state c in a range of size 2S+1 runs in time O(m (2S+1) 2^b b). For b = O(log n) and S = poly(n) this is polynomial. structure.proved_step: statement: Lemma (cofactor gate removal with free constants). For any fan-in-2 Boolean circuit C with s gates, any set I of input variables, and any assignment a in {0,1}^I, let E_a be the gates whose computed functions become constant after fixing I=a. Then C restricted by I=a has a fan-in-2 circuit of size at most s-|E_a|. Proof: traverse C in topological order, replace every gate in E_a by its constant value under the restriction, and feed that value to every consumer. Retain the other gates. The output is unchanged and each gate in E_a is removed once, including when it has multiple consumers. Consequently, for uniform a, E_a's average size is 2^{-|I|} sum_g |{a : gate g becomes constant under I=a}|.

statement: For a Boolean function f:{0,1}^X x {0,1}^Y -> {0,1}, let S be its actual X-support and A={a in {0,1}^S : f(a,.) is nonconstant}. Under a uniform assignment to X, the probability that the restricted cofactor on Y is nonconstant is exactly |A|/2^|S|. In particular, if f depends on Y then this probability is at least 2^-|S|, and this lower bound is sharp.
proof: Because f is independent of every coordinate in X\S, the restricted function f(x,.) depends only on x|_S. For uniform x in {0,1}^X, x|_S is uniform on {0,1}^S. The event that f(x,.) is nonconstant is therefore exactly the event x|_S belongs to A, which has probability |A|/2^|S|. If f depends on Y, at least one cofactor is nonconstant: otherwise all cofactors would be constant, and since f is Y-dependent this would be impossible. Thus |A|>=1. Sharpness is witnessed by f(x,y)=1[x|_S=a*] AND y, for any a* in {0,1}^S, whose nonconstant-cofactor set is the singleton {a*}.

Let w in Z^n with |w_i| <= M, let c in Z be fixed, let S subset [n] contain each i independently with probability p, and let t be uniform on [-R, R] independent of S. structure.proved_step: LEMMA (bounded integer weights, exact scope). Let w in Z^n with |w_i| <= M, let N be its support, s = |N|, and let t in Z be arbitrary. Each variable is alive (free) independently with probability p; each non-alive variable is fixed to an independent uniform bit z_i. Let g(x) = [w.x >= t]. Then E[ g is non-constant over the free variables ] <= (sqrt(2)*M + 2) * p * sqrt(s) <= (sqrt(2)*M + 2) * p * sqrt(n). PROOF. Fix the alive set A, let j = |A ∩ N|, b = s - j, and let c = sum over fixed i in N of w_i z_i. Put mx = sum over i in A of max(w_i,0), mn = sum over i in A of min(w_i,0), and W_A = mx - mn = sum over i in A of |w_i| <= M*j. Zero-weight variables affect neither c nor the window. g is non-constant iff mn + c < t <= mx + c, i.e. c in [t-mx, t-mn), a half-open interval containing exactly W_A integers. Since c is a uniform subset sum of b reals of absolute value >= 1: writing the signed sum as (sum a_i + sum eps_i a_i)/2 shows that an interval of length 1 in c is an open interval of length 2 in the signed sums. Erdos (1945) Littlewood-Offord then gives at most C(b, floor(b/2)) subsets per such interval. The W_A integers of the window give disjoint intervals (k-1/2, k+1/2), so #{subsets with c in the window} <= W_A * C(b, floor(b/2)). Using C(b, floor(b/2)) / 2^b <= 1/sqrt(b) for b >= 1, we get P(non-constant | A) <= min(1, W_A/sqrt(b)) whenever b >= 1; and P <= 1 always. AVERAGING. Case j <= s/2: then b >= s/2 >= 1 for s >= 2 (s = 1 with j = 0 has W_A = 0, probability 0). Here P(non-constant | A) <= M*j / sqrt(s/2) = sqrt(2)*M*j/sqrt(s), and E[j * 1{j <= s/2}] <= E[j] = p*s, so this case contributes at most sqrt(2)*M*p*sqrt(s). Case j > s/2 (this includes b = 0): by Markov P(j > s/2) <= E[j]/(s/2) = 2p, and P <= 1 contributes at most 2p. Summing: E <= (sqrt(2)*M + 2)*p*sqrt(s). QED. Scope: integer weights, |w_i| <= M, arbitrary threshold t, arbitrary n and p in [0,1]; the bound is per gate, so it also holds for the average over a family of gates.

structure.proved_step: LEMMA (fixed threshold, exact scope). Let w in Z^n with |w_i| <= M, t in Z fixed, S subset [n] with |S| = L, F = [n] minus S, x uniform on {0,1}^F, N = #{i in F : w_i != 0} >= 1, and l = sum over i in S of |w_i| (so l <= M L). Then P_x[ y -> [sum_{S} w_i y_i + sum_{F} w_i x_i >= t] is non-constant on {0,1}^S ] <= l / sqrt(N) <= M L / sqrt(N). PROOF. Let mx = sum_S max(w_i,0), mn = sum_S min(w_i,0), so mx - mn = l, and let c(x) = sum_F w_i x_i. The map y -> sum_S w_i y_i has min mn and max mx. Hence the function is non-constant iff mn + c < t <= mx + c, i.e. c lies in the half-open window [t - mx, t - mn), which contains exactly l integers. Zero-weight variables in F do not affect c. Let a_1..a_N be the nonzero F-weights, |a_i| >= 1. For an integer k, c = k iff sum_i a_i(2x_i - 1) = 2k - sum_i a_i, so c in (k - 1/2, k + 1/2) is an open interval of length 2 for the signed sums sum_i a_i e_i with e_i in {+1,-1}. Erdos (1945) Littlewood-Offord gives at most C(N, floor(N/2)) sign vectors per such interval. Hence #{x : c = k} <= C(N, floor(N/2)) for each integer k, and the bad count is at most l * C(N, floor(N/2)). Dividing by 2^N and using C(N, floor(N/2))/2^N <= 1/sqrt(N) gives P <= l/sqrt(N). QED. Scope: integer weights, |w_i| <= M, arbitrary t, L, N >= 1. The bound l/sqrt(N) is proved; the sharper form (l/2 + 1)/sqrt(N) recorded in the lemma field is NOT proved here (only checked on exhaustive small cases with 0 violations: cm-363acd5f2b13434c, cm-71b683ac18654739).

structure.proved_step: Switching bound (crossing form): let G be cubic bipartite with balanced cut (A,B), M0 a perfect matching, and C_1..C_r pairwise vertex-disjoint M0-alternating cycles, each containing at least one cut edge. (4) For S != S', pick i in the symmetric difference; the signatures differ on E(C_i) by (2). (5) Hence 2^r distinct signatures. Scope: cubic bipartite graphs, any balanced cut. Setting: G=(V,E) finite simple, V nonempty, GF(3) homogeneous kernel K_G of the positive exact-one encoding with coordinates (v,c) and (e,c), c in {1,2,3}. Let tau_1=(1,2,0), tau_2=(0,1,2) in T (sum-zero vectors). Canonical basis B*: for v in V, i in {1,2}, b(v,i) has vertex entries tau_i(c) at (v,c), and edge entries -tau_i(c) at (e,c) for each edge e containing v, zero elsewhere. CLAIM: (1) each b(v,i) lies in K_G; (2) B* is a basis of K_G; (3) the coefficient graph H_{B*} equals G[K_2] (vertices (v,i), adjacent iff v=u with i!=j, or uv in E); (4) hence min over bases of tw(H_B) <= tw(G[K_2]) <= 2 tw(G)+1. PROOF. (1) Vertex sums of tau_i are 0. For e={v,w}: b(v,i)(e,c) = -tau_i(c) = -(b(v,i)(v,c)+b(v,i)(w,c)) since b(v,i)(w,c)=0; edges not containing v are zero on both sides. (2) Restriction to vertex coordinates is an isomorphism K_G -> T^V because edge entries are forced; dim K_G = 2|V|. Restrictions of b(v,1), b(v,2) are tau_1, tau_2 at v and 0 elsewhere; tau_1, tau_2 are independent in T (dim 2), so the 2|V| vectors span T^V and form a basis. (3) supp tau_1={1,2}, supp tau_2={2,3}; both contain colour 2. Same vertex v: share (v,2), adjacent. uv in E: b(v,i) and b(u,j) are both nonzero at (e,2), adjacent. Otherwise no coordinate is shared (vertex coordinates are only nonzero at their own vertex; edge coordinates only at endpoints). So H_{B*} = G[K_2]. (4) Take a width-tw(G) tree decomposition (T,beta); set beta'(t)=beta(t) x {1,2}. Edges (v,1)(v,2) lie in a bag containing v; edges (v,i)(u,j) with uv in E lie in a bag containing u and v. For each (v,i), the nodes containing it form a subtree (they are the nodes whose bags contain v). Max bag size is 2(tw(G)+1), so width <= 2tw(G)+1. QED.

structure.lemma: FEW-FORMS LEMMA (repair of G0002: the memo key is replaced, not the variable order). Setting: THR o THR circuit C on n variables with m bottom gates g_j(x) = [W_j . x >= t_j], W_j in Z^n, t_j in Z, and top gate f(x) = [sum_j v_j g_j(x) >= T], v_j in Z, T in Z. Assume the rows W_j take at most d distinct values: W_j = F^{(k(j))} for a matrix F in Z^{d x n} and k: [m] -> [d], and |F_{qi}| <= B. Put R_q = sum_i |F_{qi}| <= B n and grid G = prod_q [-R_q, R_q]. Claim: #SAT(C) = #{x in {0,1}^n : f(x)=1} is computed exactly by the DP below in O(n d |G| + m |G|) integer operations, where |G| = prod_q (2R_q+1) <= (2Bn+1)^d.
structure.proved_step:
PROOF. Let s(x) = (F^{(1)} x, ..., F^{(d)} x) in Z^d, and let a_i = (F_{1i}, ..., F_{di}) be the i-th column of F. Then s(x) = sum_i x_i a_i. Since g_j(x) = [s_{k(j)}(x) >= t_j], we have f(x) = h(s(x)) with h(sigma) = [sum_j v_j [sigma_{k(j)} >= t_j] >= T]. So #SAT(C) = sum_{sigma in G} N(sigma) h(sigma), where N(sigma) = #{x : s(x) = sigma}. DP: A_0 = indicator of the origin on G; A_i(sigma) = A_{i-1}(sigma) + A_{i-1}(sigma - a_i) (entries outside G are dropped). Invariant: A_i(sigma) = #{y in {0,1}^i : sum_{l<=i} y_l a_l = sigma} for sigma in G. Induction step: a vector y in {0,1}^i with partial sum sigma either has y_i=0 (counted by A_{i-1}(sigma)) or y_i=1 (counted by A_{i-1}(sigma - a_i)). No mass is lost by the truncation to G, because every partial sum over l <= i has |coordinate q| <= sum_l |F_{ql}| <= R_q, so each partial sum lies in G. Hence A_n = N on G, and the output sum_{sigma in G} A_n(sigma) h(sigma) equals #SAT(C). Cost: the DP does n steps, each O(|G|) with d-dimensional slicing; evaluating h on a cell costs O(m). All numbers are at most 2^n, so the arithmetic is exact.

COROLLARY (sub-exponential saving). Let B be a constant and d <= n / (4 log2(2Bn+1)). Then |G| <= (2Bn+1)^d <= 2^{n/4}, so #SAT(C) is computed in time poly(n, m) * 2^{n/4} (plus the O(m d n) work to find the distinct rows), against brute force 2^n * poly(n, m). The saving is at least 3n/4 - O(log n) bits, so saving/log n -> infinity: this meets the Lemma 3.8 threshold for this subclass. Outside the subclass (d large) the bound (2Bn+1)^d is not better than 2^n and the lemma gives nothing.

SCOPE / WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED: this is a proved algorithm for the subclass 'few distinct bottom weight rows, bounded weights, d <= n/(4 log(2Bn+1))'. It does NOT handle random or general THR o THR (d = m there), so it does not repair the general memo-key obstacle. Whether the subclass is a real intermediate step (lane D / lane C, owner's intermediate-goal rule) is for review. It also does not bear on P vs NP without the general lower-bound or CAPP chain.

structure.lemma: REPAIR OF S0011 (direction and overhead). Setting: n >= 1, N = 2^n, s >= n, programs = straight-line sequences of at most s gates over {AND, OR, XOR, NOT} (NOT unary, others fan-in 2), gate k reads from the n inputs and earlier gates. Encoding: each gate = op (2 bits) + two source indices in ceil(log2(n+s)) bits, so a program is L = s(2+2ceil(log2(n+s))) = O(s log s) bits. (A) UNIVERSAL EVALUATOR: there is a Boolean circuit U_{n,s}(D, x) of size O(s(n+s)) and depth O(s log(n+s)) that outputs the value of D on x. Proof: for gate k, select each of its two operands among the n+k-1 <= n+s available values with a multiplexer tree over one-hot-decoded index bits (O(n+s) gates per operand), compute AND/OR/XOR/NOT of the two operands and select the result by op (O(1)), so each gate costs O(n+s); output selection by the last-gate index costs O(n+s). Depth per gate is O(log(n+s)) for the mux tree, so O(s log(n+s)) in total. With s >= n, size is O(s^2). (B) SEARCH-TO-DECISION: let S be a search circuit family of size M(N,s) that on input T (length N) outputs D or reject. Define DEC(T) = [D = S(T) is not reject] AND AND_{x in {0,1}^n} [U(D,x) = T(x)]. Soundness: DEC(T)=1 implies a program of at most s gates computes T, so T is in MCSP[s]. Completeness: if T is in MCSP[s], the search guarantee gives a valid D, and then DEC(T)=1. So DEC decides MCSP[s]. Size: M(N,s) + N * O(s^2) + O(N), depth: depth(S) + O(s log s) + O(log N). (C) CONSEQUENCE, correctly oriented: any decision lower bound 'every decision circuit for MCSP[s] has size > N*r(s)' gives 'every search circuit has size > N*(r(s) - O(s^2))' for the same parameters, because a search circuit of size M would give a decision circuit of size M + N O(s^2). statement: Compilation lemma (corrected sufficient condition). Let M be an oracle-free Boolean circuit of size C0 with g designated oracle gates, each receiving q input bits, and suppose each oracle gate is replaced by a Boolean circuit computing its truth table using at most a universal constant times q*2^q gates. If C0 and g are bounded by polynomials in s and q=O(log s), then the resulting oracle-free circuit has polynomial size in s. In general its size is at most C0+O(g*q*2^q). This is an upper bound only; without a lower bound for the particular oracle functions it implies no superpolynomial lower bound when q is larger.
proof: Replace each oracle gate independently by the assumed truth-table circuit. The resulting circuit size is at most C0+c*g*q*2^q for a universal constant c. If C0<=s^a, g<=s^b, and q<=K log_2(s) for constants a,b,K, then q*2^q<=K log_2(s)*s^K, so the total size is at most s^a+cK s^(b+K)log_2(s), polynomial in s. This proves sufficiency. The size estimate is an upper bound, so it supplies no lower bound for any particular oracle function and cannot establish superpolynomial size when q is only known to be large.

structure.lemma: LEMMA L-block (vertex block of the homogeneous GF(3) kernel): for T = {t in GF(3)^3 : t1+t2+t3 = 0}, every nonzero t in T has weight >= 2, hence any two nonzero vectors of T have intersecting supports. Proof: wt(t)=1 forces the coordinate sum to be a nonzero element of GF(3), contradicting t in T; two supports of size >= 2 in a 3-set have total size >= 4 > 3, so they meet. This is condition (L) of Thm 4.1 for the coordinate-blocked kernel; it does not by itself discharge G0001.
